vocabulary.meaning_en: an opinion about what someone should do
vocabulary.note_ar: غير معدودة: some advice / a piece of advice
vocabulary.note_en: Uncountable: some advice / a piece of advice.
vocabulary.example: Can I give you some advice?

vocabulary.meaning_en: do work that you should have done earlier
vocabulary.example: You have a lot of work to catch up on.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a list of jobs you need to do
vocabulary.example: I write a to-do list every morning.
Your only option is to tell the truth.

vocabulary.meaning_en: admit that you made a mistake
vocabulary.note_ar: ويقال أيضًا put your hands up
vocabulary.example: I made a mistake, so I held up my hands and apologised.

vocabulary.meaning_en: good for you; to your advantage
vocabulary.example: It might be in your interest to apply early.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a job that is free for someone to take
vocabulary.example: There's a vacancy in our department.
Take a few days off and chill out.
Don't put yourself under undue pressure.

vocabulary.meaning_en: do something too quickly without thinking
vocabulary.example: Don't rush into a big decision.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an opinion that people write about a product, hotel, etc.
vocabulary.example: Check the reviews before you book the hotel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: all sold; there are none left
vocabulary.example: Sorry, those jackets are sold out.

fine_lines.title: Make sure you do vs Make sure you don't
fine_lines.explanation_ar: make sure you + فعل = تأكد أن تفعل. make sure you don't + فعل = تأكد ألا تفعل. قد يكون المعنى واحدًا بصيغة مثبتة أو منفية.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Make sure you + verb" = remember to do it. "Make sure you don't + verb" = be careful not to do it. Often the same advice, positive or negative.

examples.sentence: Make sure you turn off the lights.
Make sure you don't leave the lights on.

fine_lines.title: Your only option is to vs You have no choice but to
words: you have no choice but to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: كلتاهما تعني أنه لا يوجد بديل آخر. بعدهما to + الفعل الأساسي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Both mean there is no other choice. Both are followed by "to + base verb".

examples.sentence: Your only option is to tell your boss.

examples.word: you have no choice but to
examples.sentence: You have no choice but to call the police.

expressions.meaning_en: Strong advice: you should have done it already. (Followed by the past simple.)
expressions.example: Isn't it about time you went to bed? You have school tomorrow.

expressions.phrase: Have you thought about the possibility of ...ing?
expressions.example: Have you thought about the possibility of changing your course?
The sooner you call the client, the better.

expressions.meaning_en: Advises the best option when there is no better choice.
expressions.example: The car won't start. You might as well take the bus.

expressions.meaning_en: Says there is only one thing to do.
expressions.example: Your only option is to tell the teacher you lost the book.

expressions.phrase: You have no choice but to ...
expressions.meaning_en: Strong advice: there is no alternative.
expressions.example: You have no choice but to call the police.

expressions.phrase: It might be in your interest(s) to ...
expressions.meaning_en: Says something will be good for the person.
expressions.example: It might be in your interest to tell them you want the job.

expressions.meaning_en: A soft, polite piece of advice.
expressions.example: You might want to call him and say you'll be late.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite suggestion to think about an option.
expressions.example: You might want to consider taking your holiday in July.

expressions.meaning_en: Reminds someone to do or not do something.
expressions.example: Make sure you don't forget your tablets.

expressions.meaning_en: Says trying costs little and could work.
expressions.example: They might still have the jacket. It's worth a try.

expressions.phrase: It might be a good idea to ...
expressions.example: It might be a good idea to check the reviews before you book.
How about joining a book club?

expressions.phrase: It's not the end of the world.
expressions.meaning_en: Says a problem is not very serious.
expressions.example: You made a mistake, but it's not the end of the world.
You have a week before the deadline. Don't rush into it.

grammar.title: It's (about) time + past simple
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد It's about time نستخدم الماضي البسيط رغم أننا نتحدث عن الآن، ويعني أن الأمر تأخّر.
grammar.explanation_en: After "It's (about) time" we use the past simple, even though we mean now. It means it should already have happened.
examples: Isn't it about time you got a haircut?
Isn't it about time you started studying?

grammar.title: Verb patterns in advice phrases
grammar.explanation_ar: the possibility of / consider / How about + ing. You might as well / might want to / make sure you + الفعل الأساسي. only option is / no choice but / in your interest / a good idea + to + الفعل.
grammar.explanation_en: the possibility of / consider / How about + -ing. might as well / might want to / make sure you + base verb. only option is / no choice but / in your interest / a good idea + to + verb.
examples: You might want to consider repeating the year.
It might be a good idea to talk to your teacher.

questions.question: Isn't it about time you ___ to bed?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد It's about time نستخدم الماضي البسيط.
questions.explanation_en: Use the past simple after "It's about time".

questions.question: Have you thought about the possibility of ___ your course?
The sooner you start, the ___ you'll feel.
You have no choice but ___ the police.
"It's worth a try" means:
choices: It could work, so try it.
questions.explanation_en: It means trying is a good idea.

questions.question: The car won't start. You might as well ___ the bus.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد might as well نستخدم الفعل الأساسي.
questions.explanation_en: After "might as well" use the base verb.

questions.question: Which phrase is the SOFTEST advice?
choices: You have no choice but to go.
Your only option is to go.
Isn't it about time you went?
questions.explanation_ar: You might want to هي الأكثر لطفًا.
questions.explanation_en: "You might want to" is the softest.

questions.question: "Hold up your hands" means:
questions.explanation_ar: hold up your hands = يعترف بخطئه.

questions.question: Make sure you ___ forget your keys.
"It might be in your interest to apply" means:
choices: Applying could be good for you.
